task: Write one sentence of your own using the word adorn. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know adorn should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Jewelers in the old quarter adorn even their doorframes with hammered tin stars.
To trim is the lightest touch of decoration — a ribbon at a cuff — stopping well short of adorn.
To festoon goes further than adorn: garlands looped from every beam until the ceiling itself disappears.

To garnish is to add a small finishing touch, almost always to a plate of food — a sprig of parsley, a twist of lemon. Adorn is broader and warmer: it dresses up rooms, clothing, or whole halls with touches meant purely for beauty, not just a chef's final flourish.

To bedeck is to drape something in finery, often to the point of excess — a hall bedecked for a jubilee looks nearly buried in it. Adorn is more restrained and deliberate: a few graceful touches added for beauty, where bedeck piles the finery on.

The staff didn't repair or rearrange the ballroom — they dressed it up, which is exactly the work adorn names.

Rather than beg for funds, the librarian, Ms.
Okafor, decided to adorn the room herself, a little at a time.
